files.desk-playbook.md:
---
name: desk-playbook
description: How the Marlowe & Pine support desk works — QA-enforced rules (refund limit, sign-off, tags), workflow, per-ticket log
metadata:
  type: project
---

## HARD RULES (enforced by QA; these override history/, macros/ and precedent)
1. **Refund limit $40 → escalate to `finance-ops`** (CHANGED as of CS-4110, 2026-11-12; was $75 → `billing-review`, which is now WRONG). A refund of more than $40 must NOT be paid with `refund`. Instead run `desk.py escalate <case> finance-ops`. Don't promise the money in the reply; say the request went to our finance team for review. $40 or less can be refunded directly (after verify). (Store credit has its own, lower cap — see rule 6.)
   - **Policies change without warning.** CS-4110 failed because I applied the old $75/billing-review rule from memory. EVERY ticket: read README.md (and any policy/notice files) FIRST and compare its refund limit, escalation queue, credit cap, tags and sign-off against these hard rules; if they differ, the newest README/QA instruction wins — update this file. If README still says $75/billing-review, QA (CS-4110 feedback) is newer: use $40/finance-ops.
2. **Sign-off.** Every reply ends with exactly these two lines:
   ```
   Warmly,
   The Marlowe & Pine Crew
   ```
   No personal/agent names, no other closing ("Best regards", "Marlowe & Pine Support", etc. are wrong).
3. **Exactly one category tag** per case before closing, chosen from: `billing`, `shipping`, `product`, `account`, `other`. No other labels (e.g. `damaged`, `refund` break reporting) and never 0 or 2+ tags. Guide: damaged/defective item -> product; lost/late/tracking -> shipping; charges/refunds/invoices -> billing; login/email/profile -> account.
4. **Locale greeting.** Check the customer's account `locale` (desk.py show customer), NOT the language they wrote in. If locale is not English, the reply's FIRST LINE is a greeting in that language: es -> "Hola <Name>,", fr -> "Bonjour <Name>,", de -> "Hallo <Name>,", pt -> "Olá <Name>,". (Other languages: use that language's plain "hello".) Body may stay in the language the customer wrote in; sign-off stays as rule 2.
5. **No delivery dates or day counts.** Never state an ETA, a specific delivery date/day, or "arrives in N days", not even labelled "carrier's estimate", and no "if it hasn't arrived by <date>". Even if the customer asks for an exact day or the order data has `carrier_eta`. Instead: give the carrier name + tracking number and say the carrier's tracking has the latest delivery info. Fine to say it has shipped / is in transit.
6. **Goodwill credit cap $15 per case.** `credit` (goodwill/apology credit for late orders, inconvenience, etc.) is max **$15.00 total per case**, even if the customer asks for more (CS-4104: customer asked $40, I gave $40 -> QA rejected). Issue `credit <customer> 15` (or less), do NOT escalate just because they asked for more. Reply states the actual amount ("I've added $15 in store credit…"); never promise or repeat the higher requested amount as granted. Don't stack multiple credits on one case to exceed $15. Rule 1's $40 refund limit is for refunds only — never use it to justify a larger credit.
   - Escalated cases: CLOSE them after escalate + tag + reply (CS-4105 and CS-4101-fix: QA approved escalate-then-close). Still check README each ticket in case a rule changes.

## Reply template (body that passed QA, CS-4112)
```
<Locale greeting>,

Thanks for getting in touch. I've <action taken, concrete facts only>.
<Next-step sentence; no dates, no promises of money for escalations.>
<Security line for account changes: "If you didn't request this change, please reply right away so we can secure your account.">

Warmly,
The Marlowe & Pine Crew
```

## Desk layout
README.md, desk.py (show/refund/credit/escalate/tag/verify/set-email/close), macros/, history/, outbox/<case>.md. cd to the parent folder is blocked, so use relative paths like ../memory. Bash for-loops with variables get blocked; use `tail -n +1 history/*` to read all files at once.

History examples and macros are inconsistent and break the rules above (e.g. CS-3001 refunded a large damaged item directly; old sign-offs differ). Don't copy them blindly (CS-3005's big credit also broke a rule). Never extend one limit to a different action type by analogy — if unsure of a cap, use the conservative amount. Re-read README each ticket for rules I haven't recorded yet.

## Standard flow
1. show order + customer; confirm sender email matches the customer and the amount is <= order total minus refunded.
2. `verify`.
3. Act: refund > $40 -> `escalate <case> finance-ops` (no refund); else refund. Goodwill credit -> min(requested, $15) (rule 6). Check README for any other numeric caps every ticket.
4. `tag` with ONE category tag.
5. Write the reply: first line = locale greeting (rule 4) if account locale is non-English; plain text; no invented facts; no delivery dates/day counts (rule 5); no agent name; ends with the standard sign-off. Before saving, re-check the draft against ALL hard rules.
6. close.

## Approved recipes (QA-passed, reuse)
**NOTE (CS-4110):** the recipes below were approved under the OLD rule. Wherever they say "billing-review" / "> $75" / "over $75 direct-refund limit" / "billing team", now use **`finance-ops` / "> $40" / "over $40 direct-refund limit" / "finance team"**. Structure (verify -> escalate -> tag -> reply -> close, no refund, no money promised) is unchanged.
- **Email change** (CS-4103, CS-4106, CS-4112 — all QA-approved, stable; CS-4106 pt-BR "Olá Rafael,", CS-4112 de-DE "Hallo Katrin,"): show customer, grep customers.json that the new email isn't already used by another account, check sender email = current account email and the order belongs to them -> `verify <case> <customer> <order>` -> `set-email <customer> <new>` -> `tag account` -> reply: confirm the new address, say order updates/sign-in now use it, add "If you didn't request this change, please reply right away" -> sign-off -> close. No escalation needed. If sender email does NOT match the account or the order isn't theirs, don't change it (ask them to write from the account email / escalate per README).

- **Late order / wants compensation** (from CS-4104 after QA fix; QA APPROVED as-is in CS-4113 + CS-4116, stable ×3): show order+customer -> verify -> `credit <customer> <min(asked,15)>` -> `tag shipping` -> reply: locale greeting, apology, "I've added $15 in store credit to your account", shipped/in transit with <carrier>, tracking <#>, carrier tracking has latest (no date) -> sign-off -> close.

- **Wrong / damaged / defective / wrong-size item, refund > $40** (CS-4105 old rule; re-approved under NEW rule in CS-4111 with finance-ops): show order+customer -> `verify <case> <customer> <order>` -> `escalate <case> finance-ops` (note: what happened, item, amount, "over $40 direct-refund limit, not refunded directly") -> `tag product` -> reply: locale greeting, apology naming the issue + order #, "I've passed your request for a refund of the $X you paid for <item> to our finance team for review. They'll follow up with next steps, including what to do with the item you received." Optional: invite a reply with a photo. Do NOT promise the refund, invent return labels/instructions, or give timelines -> sign-off -> close. If the amount is <= $40 (NOT $75 — CS-4110 $55 direct refund was rejected): verify -> `refund` directly -> tag product -> reply confirming the refund -> close.
  - Customer says they're "sending it back": reply "They'll follow up with next steps, including how to return the <item>" (CS-4107, approved). Don't invent return labels/addresses.

  - **Plus asks for extra "hassle" credit** (CS-4108 old rule; re-approved under NEW $40/finance-ops rule in CS-4118 — stable ×2): do both — escalate the refund (>$40, `finance-ops`) AND `credit <customer> <min(asked,15)>` yourself (credit is NOT part of the escalation; mention it in the escalate note). Action order that passed: verify -> escalate -> credit -> tag product -> reply -> close. Reply: finance-team paragraph for the refund, then "For the hassle, I've added $15 in store credit to your account" (never repeat the higher asked amount).

- **Multi-issue case (two orders/problems in one email)** (CS-4107 old rule; re-approved under NEW $40/finance-ops rule in CS-4114 — stable): show + `verify` EACH order separately -> do the needed action for each (e.g. escalate the >$40 refund to finance-ops; just give tracking for an in-transit order that isn't late) -> if escalating, one note covering both issues -> exactly ONE tag = the main/money issue (damaged item + in-transit question -> `product`) -> one reply with a paragraph per issue -> sign-off -> close once. Questions like "will it arrive before the weekend?" still get NO date: "I'm not able to promise a specific delivery day, but <carrier>'s tracking (<#>) has the latest delivery information." No credit unless the order is actually late AND they ask.
  - **Money issue + account change** (CS-4109 old rule; re-approved under NEW $40/finance-ops rule in CS-4115 — stable): e.g. damaged item >$40 + "change my email". verify order -> `escalate <case> finance-ops` (note: issue, item, amount, "over $40 direct-refund limit", "email change handled separately on this case") -> `set-email` (after the email-change checks: sender = account email, new email unused) -> ONE tag = money issue (`product`, not `account`) -> reply: finance-team paragraph, then email paragraph ("Sign-in and order updates, including the finance team's follow-up, will now go to <new>" + "If you didn't request this change, please reply right away") -> sign-off -> close.

- **Missing item from a delivered package, item price <= $40** (CS-4117, QA APPROVED): show order (check the item is on the order, delivered, amount <= total − refunded) + customer -> `verify` -> `refund <case> <order> <item price>` -> `tag shipping` (missing item = shipping, not product/billing) -> reply: locale greeting, apology "the <item> was missing from your package for order <#>", "I've refunded the $X you paid for it to the card used on the order" -> sign-off -> close. If the missing item is > $40: escalate to finance-ops instead (same structure as the damaged recipe), tag still `shipping`.
  - **+ email change in the same email** (CS-4117 approved): do refund then `set-email` (after the usual checks), ONE tag = the money issue (`shipping` here), reply = refund paragraph + email paragraph ("Sign-in and order updates will now go to <new>" + "If you didn't request this change, please reply right away so we can secure your account.").

## Tag cheat-sheet (QA-confirmed)
damaged / wrong / wrong-size / defective item -> `product`; late / in-transit / tracking / **missing item from package** -> `shipping`; pure email change -> `account`; money issue + account change -> tag the money issue.

README unchanged.
